message.reasoning:
Since NodeUtil is a large class, I'll focus on writing JUnit 4 tests for a solid subset of methods that offer clear branch coverage, mostly ones operating directly on Node objects using the Node and Token classes from the rhino package, matching the actual Closure-94b defect test suite as closely as possible.

I'm reviewing the Node class API from Rhino—constructors, factory methods like newString and newNumber, and child-manipulation methods like addChildToBack—to figure out how to properly build test trees with correct parent-child relationships for functions like getFunctionName. Now I'm sketching out specific test cases, starting with getBooleanValue for different node types like empty strings.

For HOOK, it's testing whether the true and false branches match to determine the boolean value, defaulting to unknown otherwise. Then I'm working through getStringValue cases for names, numbers, booleans, null and void, and finally getFunctionName's logic for deriving names from parent NAME, ASSIGN, or default child nodes.

Now I need to properly construct the node hierarchy with actual child-linking calls to test these cases realistically. I'm also mapping out getNearestFunctionName's fallback to object literal keys when a direct function name isn't found, and isImmutableValue's rules covering literals, void/negation recursion, and special names like "undefined" and "Infinity".

I'm then working through isLiteralValue (arrays/objects/regexps require all-const children, functions depend on the includeFunctions flag), isValidDefineValue's whitelist of operators and defines-set membership checks, and isEmptyBlock's handling of blocks with only EMPTY children versus other node types—setting up test cases for each before moving into simple operator type checks.

Continuing on, I'm covering associativity (MUL yes, ADD no), assignment operator detection and its mapping back to base operators (with an exception for non-assignment ops), FOR-IN structure detection by child count, loop and control structure identification, and how to extract the code block or condition expression for each construct type (IF, WHILE, DO, FOR with 3 vs 4 children, CASE), plus checks for statement blocks and statement validity requiring a non-null parent.

I'm then working through switch case detection, reference/label name validation, try-finally structure checks by comparing child count and last child, operator-to-string conversions with failure cases, valid property name checks (including ASCII-only Latin validation), precedence lookups with error handling for unknown types, object literal key detection based on even/odd index within OBJECTLIT, and finally building qualified prototype property names like "a.prototype.b" to test prototype-related helper functions.

Continuing on, I move to testing qualified name node construction—single names becoming NAME nodes and multi-part names forming GETPROP chains—along with finding the root of such chains, plus a batch of straightforward boolean type checks (isGet, isName, isNew, isCall, isThis, etc.) that are quick to verify. Then I cover function-related checks requiring proper parent context, tree traversal helpers like containsFunction and referencesThis, node construction utilities (newExpr, newFunctionNode, newVarNode, newUndefinedNode, newName), and logic for getAssignedValue and isLhs based on parent node type and position.

I continue through TRY node tests for finally/catch handling, FUNCTION node parameter extraction, constant name property checks, source name traversal, and call node free-call detection based on whether the callee is a NAME node. The biggest challenge is evaluatesToLocalValue, which has many branches (ASSIGN, COMMA, AND/OR, HOOK, INC/DEC, THIS, NAME, GETELEM/GETPROP, CALL, NEW, FUNCTION, REGEXP, ARRAYLIT, OBJECTLIT, IN, and defaults) — given the sheer scope, I need to prioritize testing the highest-value branches rather than trying to cover everything exhaustively.

Since full branch coverage across such a massive class isn't realistic, I'm focusing on writing a substantial set of tests covering most methods while noting where I'm uncertain about the exact Node API — recalling that the Closure compiler's Node class (from its Rhino fork) exposes constructors, static factory methods for strings and numbers, and various child manipulation methods like adding, retrieving, and traversing children/siblings.

I'm going through the remaining API surface: children queries, type/string/double accessors, parent access, qualified name checks, boolean/generic property getters and setters, JSDoc info, information copying, and side-effect flags including things like isNoSideEffectsCall and getAncestors. Given the complexity of side-effect-dependent methods like functionCallHasSideEffects and callHasLocalResult, I'm deciding to be selective in testing evaluatesToLocalValue's CALL branch, possibly using a simplified predicate to keep things manageable.

Tracing through the logic, I confirm that with a null compiler and default side-effect flags, callHasLocalResult returns false and locals.apply defaults to false too, so evaluatesToLocalValue works fine without needing a compiler mock. Similarly, functionCallHasSideEffects and constructorCallHasSideEffects only hit the compiler-dependent branch when dealing with GETPROP name nodes and a non-null compiler, so I can test the rest safely with null. That means mayHaveSideEffects and mayEffectMutableState are also testable this way by constructing various node trees. Given the scope, I'm planning to write a large but manageable set of test methods, aiming for something like 60-90 tests.

I'm also verifying that the Token class has all the fields I'll need for constructing these node trees -- operators, literals, control-flow tokens, and expression types like ASSIGN, CALL, NEW, GETPROP, GETELEM, and various arithmetic and comparison operators, plus statement-level tokens like IF, FOR, WHILE, TRY, SWITCH, RETURN, and THROW.

Now I'm planning out concrete test methods, starting with boolean and string value coverage (numbers, null/false/void, name-based special cases like undefined/NaN/Infinity, and default cases), then moving into expression-level boolean value tests covering assignment/comma, negation, and/or logic, and the hook (ternary) operator with matching branches.

Continuing that plan, I'll cover string value tests for names, numbers, booleans, void, and defaults; function name resolution tests (parent name/assign, default cases with and without a name); nearest function name tests including object literal keys and null cases; immutability checks across literal types, void/neg, and name-based special cases; and literal value tests for arrays, functions, and default fallbacks, wrapping up with valid declaration checks.

Then I move into isValidDefineValue tests covering literals, binary/unary expressions, and name resolution against defines; isEmptyBlock tests for block detection and children checks; simple operator type checks; associativity; assignment operator conversion including exception handling for invalid ops; for-in loop detection; loop structure and code block extraction for for/while/do loops; and control structure identification.

I continue through control structure code block variants, condition expression extraction across if/while/do/for/case statements including invalid type handling, statement block and statement checks with null parent exception handling, switch case detection, reference and label name validation, try-finally node detection, operator-to-string conversion with known/unknown handling, property name validity including Latin character checks and keyword rejection, and precedence value tests for known and unknown operators.

Now I'm covering object literal key detection with even/odd index checks, qualified name node construction for simple and multi-part names plus root extraction, prototype property detection and class/property name extraction, a batch of simple type check tests (isGet, isName, isCall, isFunction, etc.), function expression and declaration checks including hoisted function detection at script and nested scopes, and I'm starting to outline tests for containsType, containsFunction, containsCall, and referencesThis.

I'm now planning tests for newExpr, newFunctionNode, newVarNode with and without values, newUndefinedNode, and newName construction, followed by getAssignedValue tests covering var parents, assign parents where the node is or isn't the first child, and the precondition that the node must be a name. I'm also outlining isLhs tests, finally/catch block detection tests, getFnParameters, and starting on isConst tests.

Rounding out the evaluatesToLocalValue cases with function/regexp/array literals, the "in" operator, default assign-op behavior, simple operators, immutability fallback, and a case verifying an IllegalStateException throws for unhandled node types like LABEL. Then I'm moving on to checkForStateChange tests.

For mayHaveSideEffects and mayEffectMutableState, I'm covering throw statements, object literals with and without checking new object creation, var/name declarations with and without children, function expressions and declarations, constructors with and without side effects, calls to built-ins versus side-effecting functions, simple operators, and assignments to names versus getter targets.

I still need to test assignment to getters with local versus non-local literals, legacy assignment target paths, default true cases for unmatched node types like labels, and recursive checking of children. Then I'm covering constructorCallHasSideEffects and functionCallHasSideEffects tests for known/unknown constructors, non-new nodes throwing errors, built-ins without side effects, the Math namespace, unknown functions, and non-call nodes throwing errors, followed by nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects tests for assignment operators and delete property.

I'm continuing through nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects for call, new, and name nodes with and without children, plus the default case, then canBeSideEffected tests covering call/new expressions, constant versus non-constant names, known constants, get-prop/get-elem access, function expressions, and recursion. After that I'm listing tests for object call method detection, function object call/apply checks, var-args functions, and starting on callHasLocalResult tests including the throw case for non-call nodes.

For removeChild and tryMergeBlock I'm noting these are more complex tree mutation methods, so I'm picking a smaller set of key cases to cover -- statement blocks, var nodes with single versus multiple children, block and for nodes, and the invalid-throw case, plus merge block behavior for statement versus non-statement parents. I'm deciding to skip getVarsDeclaredInBranch, redeclareVarsInsideBranch, and getAddingRoot since they require complex SCRIPT/FUNCTION parent structures.

Given the sheer scope here, I'm settling on writing a large but focused test suite rather than exhaustively covering every method -- hitting most public and package-private methods with solid branch coverage, using helper builder methods, and flagging anything uncertain or skipped with comments. Now I'm thinking through how Node objects are actually constructed in this codebase, drawing on patterns from the real NodeUtilTest.

I'm weighing whether to construct Node trees manually versus parsing JS snippets through the actual parser -- using the real parser would mirror the genuine Closure test suite pattern but adds setup complexity, so I need to decide which approach keeps the tests both accurate and manageable.

Direct AST construction gives me precise control over branch conditions and edge cases that parsing wouldn't guarantee, so I'll build Node trees manually using Node's constructors and methods, relying on my recollection of the Node class API from this era of the Closure Compiler.

Still listing Node methods...

Given the uncertainty around exact method signatures, I decide to only use methods explicitly referenced in the source code itself, like getType() and getL-prefixed calls, to guarantee my tests compile correctly.

Still listing AST helper methods...

Still building node helpers...

Still confirming API usages...

Still listing more Node/NodeUtil methods... I'm noting that setting side effect flags for test purposes needs a setter that isn't visible in the NodeUtil source I'm working from.

I'll assume unset CALL/NEW nodes default to isNoSideEffectsCall() returning false, and avoid calling setters I'm unsure about — for callHasLocalResult, I'll only test the precondition exception rather than the flag-set case.

I'm double-checking constructor signatures against actual usage in the codebase, confirming variants like Node(type, left, right, lineno, charno), Node(type, lineno, charno), and Node(type, child) all exist based on how they're called elsewhere.

I've also confirmed Node.newString and Node.newNumber factory methods in both their 2-arg and 4-arg forms, plus getDouble() for retrieving numeric values. Now I need to figure out how to build nodes with more than two children, like FOR loops or ARRAYLIT with multiple elements, likely using addChildToBack repeatedly after creating the base node.

I also confirm hasOneChild, hasMoreThanOneChild, and hasChildren are available, along with getAncestors returning an Iterable<Node> for traversal, and getType returning an int comparable against Token constants. For literal nodes like TRUE/FALSE/NULL, I'll rely on the newString-style factory methods rather than assuming separate no-arg constructors.

Now I'm sketching helper methods for the test class -- small wrappers for numbers, strings, names, leaf nodes, and single/double-child nodes -- and thinking through how the Node constructors handle parent-child linkage automatically when children are passed in.

For testing getFunctionName, I'm constructing a var-declaration pattern: a FUNCTION node with an anonymous NAME child, params, and body block, attached as a child of a NAME node representing "myVar" -- so that getFunctionName can traverse up to find the variable name. Now I'm setting up a similar case for the ASSIGN parent scenario, building a qualified name node.

For a plain function declaration inside a block, the parent type falls to the default case, so it just returns the function's own name string if present. I'm setting up a test case with a named function node placed inside a block to verify getFunctionName returns "myFunc" correctly from the function's first child.

Now I'm working through getNearestFunctionName - the first case where getFunctionName already returns a name directly, so it short-circuits without touching the object literal branch. Next I need a separate test for when the function is assigned as a value in an object literal key.

For that case I'm constructing an anonymous function node with an empty name string, wrapping it inside an OBJECTLIT node paired with a string key "myKey". Since the anonymous function's parent is OBJECTLIT rather than NAME/ASSIGN, getFunctionName falls to the default branch and returns null because the name length is zero, which then lets getNearestFunctionName fall through to check the OBJECTLIT case and pull the key's string value instead.

I'm confirming that case returns "myKey" correctly, then considering a third case where a function's parent is something like CALL (e.g. an IIFE argument), which should make both getFunctionName and getNearestFunctionName return null since it doesn't match any of the handled parent types.

Now I want to test isFunctionDeclaration and isFunctionExpression, which rely on isStatement requiring a non-null parent and checking whether that parent is SCRIPT, BLOCK, or LABEL. I'm setting up a function whose parent is BLOCK to confirm isFunctionDeclaration returns true, and one whose parent is NAME (like a var assignment) to confirm isStatement is false there.

I'm also working through isHoistedFunctionDeclaration, which requires isFunctionDeclaration plus either a direct SCRIPT parent or a grandparent that's a FUNCTION node. I'm setting up two cases: one where a function declaration sits directly under SCRIPT, and another nested case where an inner function declaration lives inside an outer function's body BLOCK, checking that its grandparent resolves to the outer FUNCTION node.

To confirm the false branch works too, I'm constructing a case where a function declaration is inside a BLOCK whose parent is just another BLOCK, not SCRIPT or FUNCTION, so isFunctionDeclaration is still true but isHoistedFunctionDeclaration correctly returns false.

Next I'm turning to isEmptyFunctionExpression, testing it against a function expression with an empty body versus one with content, and confirming a plain function declaration always returns false regardless of body. Then for isVarArgsFunction, I'm building a function body containing a NAME node referencing "arguments" to verify the true case, plus a negative case where it's absent, and checking nested references are still detected properly.

So the traversal correctly skips inner function contents, confirming this test would catch real bugs in that boundary logic. Now I'm moving on to writing containsFunction, containsCall, and referencesThis using the containsType helper.

Good, that confirms containsFunction and containsCall work similarly with unrestricted nested search - I'll test both true/false cases. Time to write the actual test file with JUnit4 @Test annotations, helper builder methods for Node construction at the top, and well-organized comments, though I should double check the Token field first.

Checking token constant names against the NodeUtil source: ASSIGN, COMMA, NOT, AND, OR, HOOK, STRING, NUMBER, NULL, FALSE, VOID, NAME, TRUE, ARRAYLIT, OBJECTLIT, REGEXP, FUNCTION, BLOCK, EMPTY, SCRIPT, and various control-flow and operator tokens like IF, FOR, WHILE, VAR, and comparison/arithmetic operators.

All confirmed present since they're used directly in the given source code -- no guessing needed for token names, they're all literal from source. I also verify Node class members like FLAG_LOCAL_RESULTS, IS_CONSTANT_NAME, INCRDECR_PROP, FREE_CALL, ORIGINALNAME_PROP, SOURCENAME_PROP, and the static method tokenToName(int), plus TokenStream methods like isJSIdentifier.

I confirm TernaryValue is an enum with the expected helper methods and constants, useful for checking results in the getBooleanValue tests. Since the classpath doesn't include Mockito, I'll need to implement any needed interfaces manually as anonymous classes, and I'll skip testing isConstantByConvention since it requires a CodingConvention mock that's too complex to hand-roll for now.

For getInfoForNameNode, I'm considering simple cases: a node with no JSDoc and no parent should return null since both info and parent stay null through the checks. Testing with a null nameNode itself also short-circuits to a null result, so these are easy cases to cover without needing to construct JSDocInfo objects manually.

The branch involving a VAR parent with JSDocInfo would require building a JSDocInfoBuilder instance, which adds complexity, so I'll skip deep testing there and just note it with a comment. Given the scope, I'll finalize the list of methods to test and aim for a large test file with roughly a hundred test methods, accepting this will be lengthy but proceeding as instructed to maximize coverage.

Writing helper methods...

I'm avoiding a naming conflict with NodeUtil's own helper since the test class lives in the same package and can access package-private static methods directly without static imports, so I just need to declare the correct package and pick distinct names for my local helpers.

Given the scope is large, I'll focus on writing comprehensive test coverage for the pure checker methods since they're high-value and low-risk, plus solid branch coverage for the trickier logic like boolean value evaluation and side-effect detection, while skipping the AST-mutation heavy paths to keep this manageable.

I'm laying out the final test grouping: literal/boolean/string value checks with full coverage, function name lookups, then structural predicates like block emptiness, operator classification, loop and control structure detection, and reference/label/statement checks.

Beyond that, I'm covering basic type predicates (isGet, isName, isVar, isCall, isFunction, etc.), operator string conversions and precedence, prototype-related helpers, function analysis (containsCall, referencesThis, isVarArgsFunction), node construction utilities (newExpr, newName, newCallNode), and finally assignment/lhs and try-catch-finally helpers.

Now I'm moving into side-effect analysis: mayHaveSideEffects and its state-mutation checks, constructor/function call side effects, and whether a node type inherently carries side effects. I'm also planning light coverage for trickier structural helpers like variable-branch detection and block merging, flagging spots where I'm uncertain about exact API behavior so I don't invent functionality that isn't in the source.

I'm now working through isControlStructureCodeBlock's branch logic - checking each control structure type (FOR, WHILE, LABEL, WITH, DO, IF, CATCH) and verifying which child position determines true/false, plus confirming the default case throws when the parent isn't a recognized control structure.

Continuing to work through DO, IF, and TRY node structures, checking which children satisfy the first/last child conditions for each control structure type.

For a WHILE-type node with test and body, only the first child position matters, while DEFAULT nodes with a single body child always count as true. I also need to test that an invalid parent type like BLOCK throws IllegalStateException as expected, and that getConditionExpression on a FOR node with an unexpected child count (not 3 or 4) falls through the switch and throws IllegalArgumentException.

For the default node type case not covered in the switch, it throws IllegalArgumentException with a message about missing a condition. Then for getPrototypePropertyName, I plan to build a qualified name node like "Foo.prototype.bar" using NodeUtil.newQualifiedNameNode, trusting that Node's getQualifiedName() correctly reconstructs the dotted name from GETPROP/NAME chains since that's already used internally elsewhere.

For isPrototypeProperty, since it relies on getQualifiedName() returning null for non-qualified nodes like CALL, I should test that this returns false safely without throwing. For getPrototypeClassName, I'm tracing through how it walks up GETPROP nodes looking for the "prototype" segment, verifying it correctly returns the "Foo" NAME node when given "Foo.prototype.bar".

Now I'm working through getPrototypePropertyName's logic, which uses the qualified name string and locates the ".prototype." substring to extract the member name after it.

Then I'm testing isPrototypePropertyDeclaration: it checks whether a node is an expression statement wrapping an assignment whose target is a prototype property. I'm constructing test cases with EXPR_RESULT wrapping an ASSIGN node targeting a "Foo.prototype.bar" qualified name, verifying it returns true, then testing negative cases where the structure doesn't match.

Now I'm working through isVarDeclaration, checking whether a NAME node's parent is VAR versus something else, and moving to getAssignedValue, which requires the input to be a NAME node (throwing IllegalStateException otherwise) and returns the initializer child when the parent is a VAR declaration -- I'm building a test case like "var x = 5" to verify this behavior.

I'm also setting up the ASSIGN case, where a NAME on the left-hand side should return its sibling (the assigned value) via getNext(), and considering the edge case where the NAME appears on the right-hand side of an assignment instead, which should fall through to returning null.

That covers the redundant BLOCK-parent case sufficiently with one test. Given the time constraints, I'll keep coverage reasonable rather than exhaustive, and move on to designing tests for checkForStateChangeHelper, starting with verifying that a THROW node is flagged as having side effects.

Next I need tests for OBJECTLIT behavior — checking that mayEffectMutableState flags it true when checking for new objects, but mayHaveSideEffects returns false for an empty literal when that flag is off — and then a VAR node test to confirm it's treated as having side effects whenever it has a child.

For a bare NAME reference like "x;", getFirstChild() is typically null, so it returns false with no side effect. But if VAR's NAME child itself has a value child (the "var x = value" pattern), that gets picked up when the recursive loop processes the VAR node's children.

To specifically test the NAME branch with a child present, I realize I need to call mayHaveSideEffects directly on a NAME node that has a child attached, since the helper itself is private. Constructing that node directly and calling mayHaveSideEffects on it should hit the NAME case and return true because the child exists.

For the bare NAME case with no children, the same call falls through to the empty children loop and returns false, matching the "variable by itself" comment - and similarly an empty VAR node returns false while a VAR with a NAME child returns true. For FUNCTION, I'm testing that a function expression with checkForNewObjects=false returns false since the case returns immediately without recursing into children.

For a function declaration (parent BLOCK), isFunctionExpression is false so the check inverts to true regardless of checkForNewObjects, meaning declarations always count as having side effects since they modify the namespace - I'll reuse the function2 node built for getFunctionName tests here too.

I should build fresh local nodes per test method instead of sharing mutable state across tests. For NEW nodes, checkForNewObjects=true short-circuits to true immediately regardless of constructor; when false, I need constructorCallHasSideEffects to check if the constructor name is whitelisted (like "Array") and then examine the children/arguments for side effects, so I'll construct a NEW node with a NAME("Array") child to test that whitelisted case returns false when no side-effecting args are present.

For unwhitelisted constructors like "Foo", the call should return true directly without checking children. Then for CALL nodes, functionCallHasSideEffects should behave similarly -- if the function name is whitelisted (like "String"), it falls through to check the arguments for side effects rather than assuming true.

For CALL with an unknown function like "foo", functionCallHasSideEffects returns true immediately, so the overall test should expect true. For a Math namespace call like Math.max, since it's not modifying "this" and the namespace check identifies "Math" as safe, functionCallHasSideEffects returns false, and since there are no side-effecting arguments, the whole expression should be considered side-effect free.

I'll skip testing the isOnlyModifiesThisCall and REGEXP branches since they depend on compiler flags I'm unsure about. Then I move to simple binary operators like ADD with two number children, which recurse into children and should report no side effects. Finally, for assignment operators, assigning directly to a plain name like ASSIGN(NAME("x"), NUMBER(5)) is treated as having side effects, while assigning to a property (GETPROP/GETELEM) target needs more nested checks on whether the RHS or LHS themselves carry side effects.

Testing an assignment where the RHS is a call to an unknown function with side effects confirms the overall expression is flagged as having side effects, exercising that "check LHS/RHS" branch. Otherwise, when neither side has side effects, I check whether the base of the property target evaluates to a local value—if so, mutating a property on a locally-created object literal shouldn't count as a leaking side effect, since OBJECTLIT is always treated as local.

Now for the non-local case: when current isn't a literal, I walk down through GET nodes to find the base, then check if that base is a literal value. Testing "obj.prop = value" where obj is a plain external variable, the base resolves to NAME("obj"), and since it's not immutable and no locals function marks it local, this path returns true for local-value evaluation, meaning the check falls through to considering it a potential side effect.

I'm also considering the fallback case where the assignment target is neither a GET nor a NAME node, which needs its own test scenario to verify the legacy behavior.

I'll add around five tests covering these sub-branches: name-based assign target, RHS/LHS side effects, local versus non-local gets, and the legacy fallback. Then for the default case, I want to check something like a LABEL node that isn't handled by any of the simple operator or assignment checks, which should fall through to the final default "return true" statement.

For extra loop coverage, I should test a BLOCK containing multiple statements where one triggers the early "return true" exit inside the recursion loop, plus a BLOCK where all children are side-effect-free to confirm the loop completes and returns false. Now moving to nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects tests, I want to check assignment ops returning true and start looking at DELPROP-type cases.

For a constant NAME with IS_CONSTANT_NAME true, canBeSideEffected returns false no matter what's in knownConstants; for a non-constant NAME present in knownConstants, it evaluates to false, while a non-constant NAME absent from knownConstants gives true. GETPROP/GETELEM always return true, and FUNCTION requires the node to be a function expression via a precondition check, otherwise it throws an IllegalState error.

I'm testing both cases: a function expression yields false, while a function declaration should trigger that IllegalStateException, which is actually a nice fault-finding scenario since it exposes a real limitation in the code. For the default case, it recurses over children, so something like ADD(NUMBER, NUMBER) returns false since neither operand hits a special case, but ADD(NAME("x"), NUMBER) with x non-constant returns true early once it recurses into the NAME child.

Now I'm moving on to examine isObjectCallM next.

I'll skip testing the precondition check on chained value nodes since constructing that scenario is tricky, just noting the assumption instead. For newUndefinedNode, I need to verify the VOID type structure with a NUMBER 0 child when given a reference node, versus the simpler case with no reference and no copyInformationFromForTree call.

For newName and newCallNode, I'm testing that they produce correctly typed NAME and CALL nodes, checking string values, the ORIGINALNAME_PROP when given an original name, and that FREE_CALL is set true when the call target is itself a NAME node.

I also want to add straightforward tests for getFnParameters, hasFinally, getCatchBlock, hasCatchHandler, isConstantName, and getSourceName, since these follow directly from the API. With the scope this large, I'm going to assemble the full test file now, numbering methods logically and adding a condensed summary table afterward mapping test methods to the branches and conditions they cover.

Given the sheer number of tests, I'll group the summary table by target method rather than doing one row per test, to keep it concise per the "short table" request. I'll write the full code now as the main deliverable, then check the TernaryValue enum details before finalizing.

Writing test methods...

Confirming Preconditions.checkArgument throws IllegalArgumentException on failure, matching standard Guava behavior, and trusting that Node's single-int constructor sets the type field with no parent.

I'm settling on around 90-110 focused test methods before writing everything out. I also want to verify that Node's constructors are public since NodeUtil, being in a different package, needs to call `new Node(...)` directly, so those constructors must be accessible across packages.

This confirms the various Node constructors and factory methods like newString and newNumber are public, along with methods like getFirstChild, addChildToBack, and getChildCount, since NodeUtil relies on them cross-package.

With that confirmed, I'm ready to write out the full test file, organizing it into sections with clear comments covering each case, including the HOOK node's ternary equality check using enum equals (identity-safe by default) and constructing HOOK nodes with their three children.

This structure matches what's needed: three children with condition ignored, true value, and false value. Testing with both branches as TRUE leaves confirms equal boolean values return TRUE, while mismatched TRUE/FALSE leaves correctly yield UNKNOWN.

Now I'm moving on to writing AND/OR test cases...

I'll trust TernaryValue's AND/OR arithmetic since it's tested elsewhere, and focus my test cases on verifying NodeUtil correctly delegates to .and()/.or() with combinations like TRUE-TRUE, FALSE-TRUE, and FALSE-OR cases.

For NOT, I'll check that a TRUE leaf becomes FALSE, a FALSE leaf becomes TRUE, and an unknown NAME child stays UNKNOWN, relying on TernaryValue's documented not() semantics.

For ASSIGN and COMMA nodes, I'll test that the expression's boolean value derives from the last child—verifying a non-empty string yields TRUE and a zero yields FALSE. With that coverage solid, I'm ready to write out the final comprehensive code organized into logical sections.

Writing test class...

Setting up the JUnit4 test file with necessary imports for NodeUtil testing...

Writing helper builder functions...

I also need to sort out which methods throw preconditions exceptions versus not, and mark tests accordingly with expected IllegalStateException or IllegalArgumentException based on how each source method validates its input, like constructorCallHasSideEffects checking preconditions on the node type.

Writing test methods...

This same pattern applies to the FALSE and NULL cases as well, keeping the verification faithful to what NodeUtil actually delegates to rather than guessing string content. I also don't need to assert on error message text derived from Token.name().
